findings.problem: The main email 01 has a new subject line ('Find your sardiyon ka rang in new fabric'), but that change hasn't been saved in git yet, and none of the three group copies have it. All three still use the old subject 'Charm of Winter 2026 is here'. The same goes for groups/family-gifting/emails/01-charm-of-winter.md:1 and groups/ready-to-wear/emails/01-charm-of-winter.md:1. If you send the group versions, readers get a subject that doesn't match the final email.
findings.fix: Once you're happy with the new subject, run the personalize skill again for email 01, or copy the new subject line into all three group copies.

findings.problem: The new subject and the preview both lean on 'sardiyon ka rang' and 'find your'. Inboxes show the subject and preview side by side, so the reader sees the same phrase twice and the preview adds almost nothing.
findings.fix: Change one of the two. For example, keep this subject and rewrite the preview to talk about the fabrics or the season, or bring 'Charm of Winter 2026' back into the subject.

findings.problem: This copy goes to people who buy ready-to-wear. Line 10 even tells them there's 'no stitching to plan'. But the tip on line 16 (and the preview on line 2, 'why stitching early gives you sukoon') tells them to get to the tailor early. The email contradicts itself for this group.
findings.fix: For this group, change the tip and the preview to fit ready-to-wear. For example: ready-to-wear pieces arrive stitched, so order ahead of the wedding season and skip the tailor rush. Keep the real delivery times.

findings.problem: This copy goes to people who love unstitched fabric. The body talks to them that way ('already with your tailor', 'a cut you've planned with your tailor'), but the preview still promises 'Our favourite ready-to-wear looks'. The preview doesn't match the email or the reader.
findings.fix: Write a preview just for this group, such as 'Our favourite winter looks, from fabric to finished outfit, plus cash on delivery.' Keep it under 90 characters.
